Great to speak earlier today — thanks for walking through FinSecure's use case. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can scope the right option (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem):

Summary from call:
- Primary workload: document ingestion + real-time summarization + triggered generation for alerts.
- Throughput: ~200 concurrent requests during peak trading hours, ~5k tokens/min sustained.
- Data classification: regulated financial PII and transaction-level data; must meet FinSecure internal controls and regulator audits.

Clarifying questions:
1) Is it a hard requirement that the control plane be inside your VPC / customer-managed, or is customer-managed keys + strict tenant isolation on compute sufficient?
2) Do you need the inference deployment to be fully on-prem, or would a Private VPC (Redwood control plane + customer VPC peering or private link) be acceptable?
3) Any specific compliance artifacts we should include in our next message (SOC 2 type II, encryption attestations, network topology)?

Available for a 30-min call tomorrow between 10–12 PT if that helps.

Hi Mateo —

Thanks for the recap — that looks right. To answer your questions:
- Control plane: we prefer the control plane and management plane to be separated from a public multi-tenant control plane. Ideally we want either a customer VPC integration where control plane metadata / orchestration is within our network, or a Private deployment (VPC or on-prem).
- Customer-managed keys (KMS) are non-negotiable — all inference payloads must be encrypted with keys we control.
- On-prem is possible but adds procurement complexity; Private VPC would be preferred if it provides the same guarantees (network isolation, no shared tenancy for compute, customer KMS).

For SOC 2 and network details, please send any artifacts you can — we’ll start an internal review. I’m copying Daniel Park (procurement) for contract/PO timelines.

- Hosted API: fastest to get started but uses our shared control plane and multi-tenant control plane services; not aligned with your customer-managed KMS / VPC requirement.
- Dedicated capacity: single-tenant GPU pools and isolated compute; data at rest and in-flight encryption supported. Dedicated does not currently offer a fully customer-managed VPC for the control plane — that’s where Private differs.
- Private VPC / on-prem: provides customer VPC peering or air-gapped on-prem installs, customer KMS/HSM integrations, and a control plane that can be run inside your network (or under your VPC). This aligns most closely with the requests you listed.

I’ve attached a short one-pager that summarizes the options. If Private VPC is the direction, Marissa can walk through network/topology and KMS integration details. Rachel can provide procurement cadence and a rough pricing delta between Dedicated and Private.

Thanks for the ping — quick technical notes below:

1) Dedicated capacity:
- Provides single-tenant GPU pools (no other customers run on the same worker hosts).
- Data at rest and in-flight can be encrypted; we support bring-your-own-key for storage encryption within the Dedicated cluster.
- Limitations: control plane (orchestration, routing, billing metadata) is Redwood-managed; while we provide audit logs and strict RBAC, we do not run the control plane inside a customer VPC for Dedicated today. For some customers this is acceptable if they get keys + audit logs, but for regulatory audit requirements that mandate control plane locality, Dedicated will not be sufficient.

2) Private VPC / On-prem:
- Provides control-plane options: (a) control plane within customer VPC via private link/peering (managed by Redwood but running logically inside your network), or (b) on-prem air-gapped deployment where customer manages the control plane.
- Full KMS/HSM integrations supported; customer key rotation and EKM/HSM attestations possible.
- We can provide network diagrams, hardened NACLs, and collection of audit log formats for your compliance team.

3) Next steps / artifacts:
- Recommend a 30-min technical call to map FinSecure’s network topology and KMS requirements to either Private VPC or an on-prem package.
- I’ll attach our Private deployment architecture and a SOC 2 summary that we can share with procurement.

Attached: redwood-private-deployment-arch.pdf, SOC2-report-summary.pdf

Pricing note for Mateo / Rachel: ballpark delta is typically +30–70% for Private compared to Dedicated depending on control-plane locality and support SLAs. I’ll defer to Rachel for final numbers.
